practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution was the Representation of the People Act enacted by Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 327 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to make provisions with respect to all matters relating to elections to legislatures, including the preparation of electoral rolls, delimitation of constituencies, and all other matters necessary for the constitution of such houses. Using this power, Parliament enacted the RPA 1950 and RPA 1951.

practiceQuestions.q: The Representation of the People Act (RPA) was enacted in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: While the RPA, 1950 deals with the allocation of seats and delimitation of constituencies, the RPA, 1951 was enacted specifically in 1951 to govern the actual conduct of elections and related administrative details.

practiceQuestions.q: Which section of the RPA, 1951 deals with the registration of political parties with the Election Commission of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 contains provisions for the registration of political parties with the Election Commission of India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the time limit prescribed under Section 29A of RPA, 1951 for an association/body of individual citizens to apply for registration as a political party after its formation?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 29A(2) of the RPA, 1951, any association or body of individual citizens of India calling itself a political party shall make an application to the Election Commission for its registration within 30 days following the date of its formation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which section of the RPA, 1951 defines 'Corrupt Practices' during elections?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 123 of the RPA, 1951 outlines various activities that constitute 'Corrupt Practices', such as bribery, undue influence, appeal to religion or caste, and promotion of enmity.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Section 77 of the RPA, 1951, every political party must submit a list of star campaigners to the Election Commission within how many days from the date of notification of an election?
opts: Not explicitly given in RPA, but typically 7 days from notification (or governed by EC guidelines)
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 77 governs account of election expenses and star campaigners. The Model Code of Conduct and ECI instructions typically specify that the list of star campaigners must be provided within 7 days of notification for their travel expenses to be excluded from the candidate's expense limit.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to decide on disqualification of members of Parliament under Section 8 of the RPA, 1951 upon conviction for certain offences?
opts: It is a statutory disqualification that occurs automatically upon conviction
practiceQuestions.sol: Disqualification under Section 8 of the RPA, 1951 for criminal convictions is automatic upon conviction and does not require a separate order from the President or EC, though the EC notifies the vacancy.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum limit on election expenditure for a Lok Sabha constituency in larger states, as currently revised and governed under the RPA rules?
practiceQuestions.sol: In 2022, the Election Commission based on recommendations increased the expenditure limit for Lok Sabha candidates in larger states to Rs. 95 lakhs (and for smaller states to Rs. 75 lakhs), under the Conduct of Elections Rules framed pursuant to RPA, 1951.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Section 126 of the RPA, 1951, public meetings, processions, and display of election matter through television or similar apparatus are prohibited during what period before the end of poll?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 126 prohibits election campaign through public meetings, processions, or media (television/radio) during the 48-hour period ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll.

practiceQuestions.q: An election petition calling in question any election can be presented to which judicial forum under the RPA, 1951?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Part VI of the RPA, 1951 (Sections 80 to 122), an election petition calling in question any election to Parliament or State Legislature can be filed only in the respective High Court having jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the landmark Supreme Court ruling in 'Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013)' alter the disqualification landscape under Section 8(4) of the RPA, 1951?
opts: It upheld the protection given to sitting MPs/MLAs from immediate disqualification if they appealed within 3 months.
It declared Section 8(4) unconstitutional, thereby removing the exception that allowed convicted lawmakers to retain seats pending appeal.
It transferred the power of disqualification from the Election Commission to the Governor and President.
It made all criminal offences grounds for lifetime disqualification.
practiceQuestions.sol: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA, 1951 as ultra vires, ruling that Parliament lacked legislative competence to protect convicted lawmakers from immediate disqualification pending higher court appeals.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind Section 123(3) and 123(3A) of the RPA, 1951 prohibiting appeals to religion, race, caste, community, or language during election campaigns?
opts: To restrict political parties from fielding candidates from minority communities
To uphold the secular fabric of Indian democracy and prevent polarization along divisive identity lines
To ban all religious organizations from registering as political parties
To ensure that all candidates use only national language in their manifestos
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 123(3) and (3A) treat appeals to religion, race, caste, community, or language, or the promotion of feelings of enmity/hatred between different classes as corrupt practices, safeguarding the secular principles enshrined in the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the RPA, 1951 handle the requirement of domicile for contesting elections to the Rajya Sabha from a particular state, following legislative amendments in 2003?
opts: Domicile in the state was made strictly mandatory for all candidates.
The requirement of being an elector in that specific state was removed, allowing any Indian citizen to contest from anywhere.
The requirement of being an elector (registered voter) in that state was retained, but the 'domicile' requirement (living in the state) was abolished.
Only persons born in that state can contest Rajya Sabha elections from there.
practiceQuestions.sol: In 2003, Parliament amended the RPA, 1951 to remove the 'domicile' requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates, meaning a candidate no longer needs to be a resident of the state they represent, but they must still be registered as an elector anywhere in India (previously they had to be an elector in that specific state, which was also relaxed to any state in India).

practiceQuestions.q: What significant change was introduced in Rajya Sabha elections through the open ballot system under the RPA, 1951 amendments in 2003?
opts: General public was allowed to vote in Rajya Sabha elections.
MLAs have to show their marked ballot paper to the authorized party agent before casting, to curb cross-voting and horse-trading.
Votes can now be cast online through electronic voting machines.
Secret ballot was replaced by a completely anonymous digital platform for MLAs.
practiceQuestions.sol: To check rampant cross-voting and corruption in Rajya Sabha elections, the RPA, 1951 was amended in 2003 to introduce an open ballot system. MLAs must show their ballot paper to their party's authorized observer before putting it in the ballot box.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the RPA, 1951, what happens if a candidate fails to lodge an account of election expenses within the stipulated time and manner?
opts: Only a monetary fine is imposed by the District Collector.
The candidate is disqualified for a period of up to 3 years from the date of order.
The election of the winning candidate is automatically declared void without petition.
The political party to which the candidate belongs is derecognized.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 10A of the RPA, 1951 provides for the disqualification of a person for failure to lodge an election expense account within the time and manner required by law. Such a person can be disqualified for up to 3 years by the Election Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: Which amendment to the RPA, 1951 introduced the 'NOTA' (None of the Above) option on EVMs/ballot papers following a Supreme Court directive?
opts: Implementation was done by the ECI pursuant to Supreme Court judgment in People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v. Union of India (2013)
Section 79(f) explicit statutory amendment by Parliament in 2010
practiceQuestions.sol: NOTA was introduced pursuant to the Supreme Court's landmark judgment in PUCL v. Union of India (2013), directing the ECI to provide a NOTA button on EVMs to enable voters to exercise a negative vote.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the RPA, 1951, what is the legal consequence if a candidate contests an election from more than the permitted maximum number of constituencies (currently set at 2)?
opts: All nominations of the candidate are rejected automatically.
Under Section 33(7), a candidate can contest from a maximum of two constituencies, preventing multiple entries.
The candidate faces a lifetime ban from electoral politics.
The political party sponsoring them is fined 10 lakh rupees.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951 was amended in 1996 to restrict a person from contesting from more than two constituencies for the same office in general or bye-elections.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the key objective of introducing Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) systems, which are integrated into the electoral process under statutory rules of RPA, 1951?
opts: To enable remote voting for migrant workers
To provide physical confirmation to voters that their vote has been cast correctly to the intended candidate, ensuring transparency and auditability
To replace electronic voting machines entirely with paper ballots
To calculate election results within 2 hours of poll closure
practiceQuestions.sol: VVPAT allows voters to verify their votes through a slip generated by the printer, which displays the candidate's name and symbol, enhancing transparency and voter confidence in EVMs.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Section 33B (which was inserted and subsequently struck down) and general provisions of RPA, 1951, disclosure of criminal antecedents by candidates has evolved through Supreme Court mandates. What is the current requirement?
opts: Candidates are only required to disclose convictions, not pending criminal cases.
Candidates must publish information about their pending criminal cases in newspapers and TV channels thrice during the campaign period.
Candidates with any pending criminal case are completely barred from contesting.
Criminal disclosures are strictly confidential between the candidate and the Returning Officer.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following Supreme Court directions (Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India, 2018 and subsequent orders), candidates and political parties must widely publicize pending criminal cases in newspapers and electronic media multiple times during elections.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the RPA, 1951 address the issue of booth capturing?
opts: It is not addressed in RPA, 1951; it is solely an IPC offense.
Section 135A defines booth capturing as a specific electoral offense and prescribes penal consequences.
Booth capturing automatically leads to the disqualification of the Prime Minister/Chief Minister.
It allows the Returning Officer to declare the winning candidate of that booth as runner-up.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 135A was inserted into the RPA, 1951 in 1989, explicitly defining 'booth capturing' as an electoral offense punishable with imprisonment and fine, and empowering the ECI to countermand polls.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Representation of the People Act (RPA), 1951:
1. It regulates the actual conduct of elections and bye-elections in India.
2. It contains provisions relating to the qualification and disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures.
3. It lays down procedures for the settlement of election disputes through Election Tribunals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct as RPA 1951 governs election conduct. Statement 2 is correct as it outlines qualifications and disqualifications. Statement 3 is incorrect because Election Tribunals were abolished by an amendment in 1966, and election petitions are now filed directly in the respective High Courts.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disqualification of lawmakers under Section 8 of the RPA, 1951:
1. A person convicted of any offense and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years is disqualified from the date of conviction.
2. Persons convicted of certain specific crimes like untouchability, dowry, and sati are disqualified even if the imprisonment is less than two years.
3. The disqualification ceases immediately if the convicted lawmaker files an appeal in a higher court within 90 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Section 8 mandates disqualification for 2+ years imprisonment sentences, and lists specific offenses where lesser or any imprisonment duration triggers disqualification (e.g., Protection of Civil Rights Act, Dowry Prohibition Act). Statement 3 is incorrect; following the Lily Thomas judgment (2013), filing an appeal does NOT stay the disqualification unless the conviction itself is stayed by an appellate court.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding registration of political parties under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951:
1. The Election Commission of India has been explicitly empowered by the Act to derecognize a registered political party on grounds of internal democracy deficit.
2. Every political party registered under Section 29A must bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the RPA, 1951 does not empower the ECI to derecognize political parties on grounds of lacking internal democracy (the ECI has repeatedly sought this power from Parliament). Statement 2 is correct as Section 29A(5) mandates that the application for registration must state that the party bears true faith and allegiance to the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding election expenses under the RPA, 1951:
1. The expenditure limit applies to the expenses incurred by the candidate from the date of their nomination to the date of declaration of result.
2. Expenses incurred by leaders of a political party whose names are communicated as 'star campaigners' are excluded from the candidate's individual election expense limit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 77 and related rules cover election expenses from the date of notification/nomination till declaration, and explicitly exempt travel and general campaign expenses incurred by recognized star campaigners from individual candidate limits (provided they do not take a specific candidate's name exclusively).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding electoral offenses under Chapter III of Part VII of the RPA, 1951:
1. Promoting enmity between different classes in connection with election on grounds of religion, race, caste, community, or language is categorized as a corrupt practice under Section 123.
2. Hiring or procuring vehicles by a candidate for free conveyance of voters to and from the polling station is a corrupt practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 123(3A) covers promotion of enmity, and Section 123(5) covers the hiring or procuring of vehicles for the free conveyance of voters as corrupt practices.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the publication of criminal records by candidates under RPA, 1951 framework:
1. The Supreme Court mandated that political parties must upload details of pending criminal cases of their selected candidates on their website and social media handles.
2. This disclosure must be made within 48 hours of selection of the candidate or within 2 weeks of the nominations, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements reflect the guidelines issued by the Supreme Court in contempt petitions and directions enforcing transparency in candidate selection under the broader framework of electoral reforms connected to RPA provisions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualification on grounds of 'office of profit' under the RPA, 1951 and Constitution:
1. The term 'office of profit' is comprehensively defined in the body of the RPA, 1951.
2. The Parliament is empowered to declare by law that a particular office shall not disqualify its holder from being chosen as or being a member of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the term 'office of profit' is NOT defined in either the Constitution or the RPA, 1951; its interpretation has evolved through judicial pronouncements. Statement 2 is correct; Article 102(1)(a) and Article 191(1)(a) of the Constitution (supplemented by statutory provisions) empower Parliament and State Legislatures to exempt certain offices.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the conduct of polls and exit polls under the RPA, 1951:
1. Section 126A prohibits conducting exit polls and publishing or publicizing their results during the period notified by the Election Commission.
2. Violation of the exit poll prohibition can attract imprisonment for up to two years and/or a fine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 126A was inserted in 2010 to regulate exit polls, prohibiting them from the time elections begin until the final phase concludes. Violation carries a penalty of up to 2 years imprisonment or fine or both.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding nomination of candidates under the RPA, 1951:
1. A candidate contesting an election from a general constituency must be an elector for any parliamentary constituency in India.
2. For reserved seats (Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes), the candidate must be a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and must be an elector for any parliamentary constituency in India, not necessarily the same reserved constituency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate representations of Section 4 and Section 5 of the RPA, 1951. For Lok Sabha, a candidate needs to be an elector anywhere in India. For reserved seats, they must belong to the specified SC/ST community and be registered as an elector anywhere in India (amended in 2003, previously they had to be from that state).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding election petitions and trial under Part VI of the RPA, 1951:
1. An election petition can be filed by any citizen of India, regardless of whether they were a voter or candidate in that specific constituency.
2. The High Court trial of an election petition must be tried as expeditiously as possible and endeavor should be made to conclude it within six months from the date on which the election petition is presented to the High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because under Section 81 of the RPA, 1951, an election petition can be presented only by a candidate at such election or an elector from that constituency, not any random citizen. Statement 2 is correct; Section 86(7) stipulates that the trial of an election petition shall, as far as practicable, be concluded within six months from the date of presentation.
